holidays.name: National Lost Penny Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the humble one-cent coin. Check your couch cushions, car seats and coat pockets, and give any stray pennies a new home. If you spot one on the sidewalk, you can pick it up for luck.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance that falls on Abraham Lincoln's birthday. Lincoln's portrait appears on the U.S. penny, which links the two.
holidays.funFact: Lincoln became the first real person to appear on a circulating U.S. coin when the Lincoln cent debuted in 1909. That was the 100th anniversary of his birth.

holidays.name: National Plum Pudding Day
holidays.description: A day for the classic steamed holiday dessert. Despite the name, traditional plum pudding is a dense, spiced mix of dried fruits, suet and warm spices. It is often doused in brandy and set aflame for a dramatic finish.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. The dessert itself goes back to medieval England, where it began as a savory porridge called pottage.
holidays.funFact: Traditional plum pudding usually contains no plums. In old English cooking, 'plum' was a word for raisins and other dried fruit.

holidays.name: Darwin Day
holidays.description: A global celebration of science, curiosity and the life of naturalist Charles Darwin. Fans mark it with lectures, museum events, cake and a good deal of appreciation for barnacles, finches and beetles.
holidays.origin: Darwin was born on February 12, 1809. Science and humanist groups began organizing Darwin Day events in the 1990s to honor his birthday and promote scientific literacy.
holidays.funFact: Darwin was born on the same day as Abraham Lincoln, February 12, 1809. They were born only hours apart, on opposite sides of the Atlantic.
